# Leak Sanitizer suppressions for OloEngine
#
# Third-party libraries that intentionally leak (global singletons, etc.)
# Add entries here to suppress known false positives from dependencies.
#
# Format: leak:<function_or_module_pattern>
#
# See: https://clang.llvm.org/docs/AddressSanitizer.html#suppressing-memory-leaks

# Mono runtime allocates global state that lives until process exit
leak:mono_

# GLFW allocates X11/Wayland display state that persists
leak:glfwInit

# Mesa/NVIDIA driver global state
leak:libGLX
leak:libEGL

# Task system singletons (scheduler, event pool) — intentional process-lifetime allocations
leak:FScheduler
leak:FSchedulerTls
leak:TEventPool
leak:TLazySingleton
leak:LowLevelTasks

# GameNetworkingSockets / protobuf / crypto — global state not fully cleaned up on exit
leak:GameNetworkingSockets
leak:SteamNetworkingSockets
leak:google::protobuf
leak:libprotobuf
leak:libcrypto
leak:libsodium
leak:libssl

# Mesa radeonsi (the self-hosted AMD box, gpu-sanitizers-amd.yml). The driver
# lives in libgallium-*.so, not in a library named after it, and allocates
# process-lifetime state (screen, winsys, LLVM/ACO compiler pools, the amdgpu
# device handle) that it never frees. A leak whose ALLOCATING frame is inside
# the driver module is the driver's and is suppressed here; an engine-side GL
# leak (a texture or buffer the engine created and never deleted) still
# reports, because its allocating frame is in the engine, not in the driver.
# libGLX / libEGL above cover the loader; these cover what it loads.
leak:radeonsi
leak:libgallium
leak:amdgpu
